newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-ZICKLER FIRES BAYERN TO TOP OF BUNDESLIGA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZICKLER FIRES BAYERN TO TOP OF BUNDESLIGA.

text.p: Alexander Zickler's goal after just 15 seconds gave Bayern Munich a 1-0 home win over Werder Bremen on Saturday and catapulted them back to the top of the Bundesliga.

Ruggiero Rizzitelli provided a perfect cross for Zickler, who headed past Bremen goalkeeper Oliver Reck to notch his third goal within a week. The 23-year-old forward also scored both Bayern's goals in their 2-0 win over Karlsruhe last Sunday.
The latest win moved Bayern above Borussia Dortmund, who went top on Thursday after beating St Pauli 1-0.
Bayer Leverkusen also moved above Dortmund and into second place thanks to a 2-0 win over UEFA Cup semifinalists Schalke.

"The win was very important for us," Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni said. "We deserved it because of our performance in the first half. I suffered a bit in the second half, because we lost our flow in the middle of the field."
Bremen coach Hans-Juergen Doerner said: "The goal caught us cold. We showed we can play after that. We played well and tried to go forward. But we couldn't produce the final pass."

Zicker's lightning strike came just a week after Borussia Moenchengladbach striker Martin Dahlin also notched up a goal after 15 seconds. The two now jointly hold the record for the third-fastest goal in Bundesliga history.
International striker Ulf Kirsten put Leverkusen ahead against Schalke in the 63rd minute with his 13th goal of the season. A memorable backheeler from Dutchman Eric Meijer sealed the victory.
Leverkusen are two points behind Bayern and a point ahead of third-placed Dortmund. VfB Stuttgart drop to fourth after a 1-1 draw with 1860 Munich on Thursday.
Moenchengladbach continued their climb away from the relegation zone, building on a surpise win over Dortmund last week with a solid 2-0 triumph over Fortuna Duesseldorf.

A first-half penalty from Romanian international Ion Lupescu put Moenchengladbach ahead and Swede Jorgen Pettersson added a second to put the game beyond the reach of relegation-threatened Duesseldorf.
Bottom club Freiburg look certain for the drop after going down 3-1 to fellow strugglers Hansa Rostock. They are now nine points adrift from second-bottom St Pauli.
"Hansa Rostock deserved to win this game," dejected Freiburg coach Volker Finke admitted. "We simply made too many defensive mistakes."
